title: Amazon APEX: How Patent Owners and Sellers Should Prepare
summary: Understand Amazon APEX eligibility, costs, deadlines, defenses, and outcomes, with practical preparation steps for patent owners and accused sellers.
body_markdown:
An Amazon APEX notice turns a patent dispute into a fast decision about whether an Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) stays live. Patent owners gain leverage without first filing suit. Sellers face a short response window and a narrow defense record. The hard part is deciding whether this private process fits the claim, the evidence, and the business risk. Here is how APEX works, what each side must prove, and how a marketplace dispute can spill into federal court.


## Key takeaways


- Amazon Patent Evaluation Express (APEX) addresses claims that products on Amazon.com infringe a U.S. utility patent. An evaluation addresses one patent claim, with listing and seller limits set by the operative agreement.
- An accused seller generally has three weeks to participate, resolve the dispute with the patent owner, or file a declaratory judgment action. Inaction leads Amazon to remove the accused listings.
- Each participating party submits a $4,000 deposit to the evaluator. In a single-seller merits decision, the winner gets its deposit back and the losing party funds the evaluation; multiple-seller and mixed outcomes have different allocations.
- The evaluator decides whether the patent owner is likely to prove that the accused product infringes. Ordinary invalidity arguments, discovery, live testimony, damages, and marketplace-wide injunctions fall outside the process.
- The best APEX record is an element-by-element claim chart built from dated, version-specific product evidence. General resemblance between products is not enough.
- Patent owners must assess forum risk before filing. Under *SnapRays v. Lighting Defense Group* , an APEX request may support personal jurisdiction in the accused seller's home forum.


## What is Amazon APEX?


Amazon APEX is a confidential, written procedure for resolving certain utility patent infringement claims involving third-party listings on Amazon's U.S. store. A patent owner or authorized representative identifies an asserted claim and the accused ASINs. If a seller participates, an outside patent attorney selected as the neutral evaluator reviews the parties' papers and makes a yes-or-no recommendation on likely infringement.


Amazon then acts on that recommendation. A finding for the patent owner usually results in removal of the accused listing. A finding for the seller leaves the listing in place. The result governs Amazon's treatment of the identified listing, subject to later litigation, settlement, or another legal proceeding. It does not award damages, invalidate a patent, or create precedent.


Amazon calls APEX voluntary. A seller can decline to sign the agreement, but Amazon generally removes the challenged ASIN when the seller takes no other qualifying action within the response period.


APEX term Current framework


Eligible right Active U.S. utility patent


Scope One asserted claim; ASIN and seller limits in the operative agreement


Decision Whether the patent owner is likely to prove infringement


Seller response window Generally three weeks from Amazon's notice


Evaluator deposit $4,000 from each participating party


Record Written submissions, with no discovery or hearing


Marketplace result The accused ASIN remains or is removed


Issues left unresolved Damages, a general injunction, most validity defenses, and liability outside Amazon


Design patents, trademarks, copyrights, foreign patents, and expired utility patents do not qualify for APEX. Amazon also may decline or suspend an evaluation when litigation involving the patent is pending.


## How the Amazon APEX process works


The[Federal Circuit's description of APEX](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1184.OPINION.5-2-2024_2311637.pdf) describes the procedure used in that dispute: one claim, up to 20 listings, three seller response paths, and removal after three weeks if the seller takes no action. That historical description should not replace the current agreement. Confirm ASIN limits, eligible sellers, response dates, and payment terms in the documents Amazon sends for the evaluation.


The Federal Circuit summarized the APEX process in its precedential SnapRays opinion.


### 1. The patent owner selects a claim and accused ASINs


The owner starts in Amazon Brand Registry's Report a Violation tool, as described in[Amazon's program guidance](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/seller-forums/discussions/t/03705c02-af92-400b-96a9-fbe3a2833497?mons_sel_locale=en_US) . The account must have the appropriate Rights Owner or Registered Agent role. The request identifies the patent, one claim for evaluation, and the accused ASINs within the limits of the operative agreement.


This selection deserves substantive review before submission. A claim that looks broad can carry a difficult construction or an element that public product materials never establish. Each ASIN also needs its own evidentiary read. Similar listing photos do not prove that two products have the same internal architecture or operation.


### 2. Amazon screens the request


Amazon reviews the patent and report for program eligibility. Its published requirements exclude design patents, non-U.S. patents, and expired patents. Amazon states that a court or International Trade Commission order finding infringement of the patent makes it ineligible for this program. Pending litigation can also cause Amazon to decline or suspend an evaluation.


Amazon's initial review can take several weeks.[Published guidance from Amazon](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/seller-forums/discussions/t/184cea29-7b2e-45a8-b6a5-5c7dbc42a92d?postId=3db3d1db-e621-4f5e-9c4c-dd360e3a82f3) describes four to six weeks for the initial review. A contested evaluation may bring the total to about 12 to 14 weeks.


### 3. Amazon notifies the accused seller


The seller generally receives the patent number, asserted claim, accused ASINs, APEX Agreement, and response instructions. The notice creates four practical choices:


1. **Participate.** Sign the agreement, provide the requested seller information, pay the deposit, and submit a noninfringement response.
2. **Resolve the claim.** Negotiate a retraction, license, design change, sell-through arrangement, or other settlement with the patent owner.
3. **File in federal court.** Seek declaratory relief and give Amazon the complaint within the notice period. Amazon notices filed in court have stated that the listings may remain while that lawsuit proceeds.
4. **Take no action.** Amazon removes the accused listings without an evaluator reaching the merits.


Before the deadline, counsel needs time to read the patent, identify the actual accused product version, chart the claim, and evaluate the economics of each path.


### 4. The parties fund the evaluation


Once a seller opts in, Amazon selects an evaluator and directs the parties to send the evaluator their deposits. A[publicly filed version of the APEX Procedure](https://insight.rpxcorp.com/litigation_documents/15875204) gives each side one week to pay. Confirm the payment deadline in the operative instructions. If the patent owner does not pay, the evaluation ends. If a participating seller does not pay, Amazon removes that seller's listings.


The $4,000 deposit excludes attorney fees, technical analysis, product testing, and evidence collection. It is the floor for a contested matter, rather than its full cost.


### 5. The parties brief infringement


The typical written schedule gives the patent owner 14 days for its opening submission, the seller 14 days to respond, and the patent owner seven days for an optional reply. The evaluator then generally has 14 days to decide. The actual dates and page limits come from the evaluator's schedule and the operative procedure.


There is no discovery or evidentiary hearing. A clear manual excerpt, annotated product photograph, teardown, specification, or test record can carry more weight than pages of unsupported characterization.


### 6. Amazon applies the result


In a single-seller evaluation, a likely-infringement finding leads to removal of the affected ASINs and return of the patent owner's deposit. If the owner does not carry its burden, the listings remain and the seller's deposit is returned. The losing side funds the evaluator. Multiple-seller cases, mixed outcomes, settlement, and withdrawal have different payment allocations; do not assume every deposit is refunded in full or retained by the evaluator.


A successful patent owner may receive an APEX ID for later reports concerning the same utility patent. That can make follow-on enforcement more efficient, but it does not eliminate the need to map a materially different product or design-around to the claim.


## What can the evaluator decide?


The evaluator's main question is whether the accused product likely infringes the asserted claim. Literal infringement requires every limitation; if the owner relies on the doctrine of equivalents, counsel should address it under the operative procedure rather than assume a missing literal element ends the inquiry. That inquiry can require claim construction, review of the specification and prosecution history, and a close comparison with the correct product version.


The seller has three principal routes to a favorable outcome:


- **Noninfringement.** At least one claim limitation is absent, or the owner's proposed construction does not hold under the intrinsic record.
- **A prior formal ruling.** A court, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, or the International Trade Commission has already found the relevant patent claim invalid or unenforceable.
- **Qualifying prior sale evidence.** The accused product, or a physically identical product, was on sale at least one year before the patent's earliest effective filing date, supported by evidence the evaluator can independently observe.


The third route is narrower than a full invalidity case. A seller generally cannot combine references to argue obviousness, develop an enablement challenge, or use discovery to prove inequitable conduct inside APEX. If validity is the central issue, counsel must assess a district court action, inter partes review, ex parte reexamination, or another formal proceeding. Starting a patent-office challenge does not automatically pause APEX.


The chart should state the governing construction for each disputed term, map product features to each limitation, and link every proposition to evidence. Patent owners need a complete affirmative mapping. Sellers need to identify the weakest required limitation and support the gap with the same discipline.


## How patent owners should prepare an APEX request


### Choose the claim for proof, not appearance


The best asserted claim can be proven from accessible evidence with few serious construction disputes. Compare candidate claims across four questions:


- Can public materials or a purchased sample establish every limitation?
- Does the prosecution history narrow a term that initially looks broad?
- Does the product require testing or reverse engineering to prove an internal function?
- Is the same claim defensible if the seller files in district court?


### Lock the product identity and evidence date


Preserve the listing, seller name, ASIN, model number, variations, images, manuals, and product page as they existed when reviewed. Buy a sample when the physical product matters, and record the order, packaging, labels, firmware, and test conditions. Marketplace listings change. Evidence from a later version can break an otherwise sound mapping.


### Build the chart before triggering the notice


An APEX filing can force the dispute into a seller's response window and invite a declaratory judgment action. The owner should have a review-ready evidence-of-use chart, claim-construction position, and forum-risk assessment before pressing submit.

## What accused sellers should do after receiving a notice


### Preserve first, then respond


Save the complete notice and attachments with their original timestamps. Export the live listing and variation data. Preserve manuals, supplier specifications, purchase records, samples, firmware versions, and historical product pages. Then match each accused ASIN to the product actually sold during the relevant period.


Changing or deleting the listing does not answer the allegation and can make the record harder to reconstruct.


### Run an element-by-element analysis


Start with the asserted claim, rather than the patent's abstract or drawings. Break it into limitations and map each one to the accused product. Mark evidence as confirmed, disputed, or missing. Then read the specification and prosecution history for constructions, disclaimers, and amendments that affect the disputed limitations.


A one-line response that the products are “different” gives the evaluator little to decide. A useful noninfringement chart identifies the missing element, states why it is required, and cites the product evidence that establishes the actual design or operation.


### Choose the forum based on the business objective


Seller path Usually fits when Main tradeoff


Participate in APEX A focused noninfringement position exists and the listing value justifies the deposit and defense cost Fast, narrow review with limited defenses and no internal merits appeal


Negotiate A license, design change, retraction, or commercial resolution costs less than disruption Settlement may leave the patent and broader exposure in place


File for declaratory relief Validity, broader noninfringement, or long-term freedom to operate justifies federal litigation Much greater cost, duration, and potential damages exposure


Accept removal The ASIN has low remaining value or defense economics do not work Loss of the listing without a merits determination


The listing's contribution margin, inventory exposure, remaining product life, design-around time, and effect on other channels should drive the decision. The legal position is one input.


## APEX can create federal-court risk for both sides


APEX is designed around a marketplace remedy, but its effects increasingly reach federal court. Bloomberg Law identified[140 APEX-related lawsuits](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/amazon-patent-pseudo-court-can-halt-sellers-with-scant-oversight) filed from 2019 through 2025 and found that annual filings grew by more than 200% from 2022 to 2025.


The most important venue decision is *SnapRays LLC v. Lighting Defense Group LLC* . Lighting Defense Group submitted an APEX Agreement targeting a Utah seller's listings. The Federal Circuit held that the patent owner had purposefully directed extra-judicial enforcement activity at Utah because removal would affect the seller's sales there. That supported specific personal jurisdiction in Utah. The Supreme Court[denied review](https://www.supremecourt.gov/search.aspx?filename=/docket/docketfiles/html/public/24-524.html) in March 2025.


The practical point is direct. A patent owner cannot assume that sending an APEX request to Amazon in Washington preserves its preferred forum. Before filing, counsel should assess where each targeted seller operates and whether the intended takedown effects could support jurisdiction there.


Sellers also need a clear-eyed view of declaratory judgment litigation. Filing suit can preserve sales while the case proceeds, but it opens a full patent case. Validity defenses and discovery become available, along with infringement counterclaims, damages, and a longer record. A complaint used only to delay removal can create risk far beyond the original ASIN.


## When APEX is the right tool


APEX fits when the dispute is concentrated on Amazon's U.S. marketplace, one utility patent claim has a strong mapping, the features can be proven in writing, and listing removal is the desired remedy.


Federal litigation fits better when the owner seeks damages or cross-channel relief, discovery is needed, several patents or claims matter, or validity requires a complete record. Patent-office proceedings address validity rather than whether an Amazon listing stays live. Each path solves a different problem.


Choose the forum after completing the claim chart. APEX compresses the schedule and narrows the issues. It still demands precise claim construction, product identification, and source-grounded evidence.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can an Amazon seller use prior art in APEX?


Only in a narrow way. The seller may rely on a prior formal invalidity or unenforceability ruling, or independently observable evidence that the accused product or a physically identical product was on sale at least one year before the patent's earliest effective filing date. Ordinary anticipation and obviousness presentations generally fall outside APEX.


### Can an APEX decision be appealed?


APEX has no ordinary internal appeal on the merits. A party can still pursue relief in federal court, and Amazon will follow qualifying court orders, settlements, and other legal developments that affect the listing or patent.


### How long does Amazon APEX take?


Amazon's published guidance describes an initial four-to-six-week review and as much as eight additional weeks when a seller participates, for about 12 to 14 weeks total. The operative notice and evaluator schedule control the actual deadlines.
